answer: Because the comet ledger attributes every share, the knoll audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the ripple fee twice and still divides one payout. Only 41% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not forfeit. That is 20 dollars per alias.
